preconditions.description: The input integer n is within the range [1, 5*10^5].

postconditions.description: The program outputs either 'First' or 'Second' as the chosen player.

postconditions.expression: choice == 'First' and all(1 <= p_i <= n for p_i in pairs) and all(pairs.count(k) == 2 for k in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: If playing as First, the output pairs array has length 2n, contains values in [1, n], and every pair index from 1 to n appears exactly twice.

postconditions.expression: choice == 'First' and not any(sum(chosen) % (2 * n) == 0 for chosen in all_valid_choices(pairs, n))
postconditions.description: If playing as First, there exists no selection of one element from each pair such that the sum is divisible by 2n. (Here all_valid_choices generates all possible selections of one element per pair based on the pairs array).

postconditions.expression: choice == 'Second' and len(selected) == n and all(selected.count(x) == 1 for x in selected) and all(selected[i] in pair_elements(pairs, i+1) for i in range(n)) and sum(selected) % (2 * n) == 0
postconditions.description: If playing as Second, the output selected array has length n, contains distinct numbers, each number belongs to a different pair defined by the input pairs array, and the sum of selected numbers is divisible by 2n.
The final integer read from stdin is 0, indicating the interactor accepted the solution.
